text: Inside the Strain. What happens inside a hamstring after a strain, from second zero to month six and beyond.
spoken: Inside the Strain. What happens inside a hamstring after a strain, from second zero to month six and beyond.

text: Most of this cellular timeline comes from rodent models. Human healing follows the same sequence, but probably runs more slowly, especially in larger injuries.
spoken: Most of this cellular timeline comes from rodent models. Human healing follows the same sequence, but probably runs more slowly, especially in larger injuries.

text: Skeletal muscle is built like a cable inside a cable inside a cable.
spoken: Skeletal muscle is built like a cable inside a cable inside a cable.

text: The epimysium, the deep fascia, wraps the whole muscle.
spoken: The epimysium, the deep fascia, wraps the whole muscle.

text: Perimysium wraps each bundle of fibers (fascicle). Endomysium wraps each individual fiber.
spoken: Perimysium wraps each bundle of fibers, fascicle,. Endomysium wraps each individual fiber.

text: Between fascial layers, a hyaluronan-rich loose connective tissue, made in part by fasciacytes, lets the layers glide.
spoken: Between fascial layers, a hyaluronan-rich loose connective tissue, made in part by fasciacytes, lets the layers glide.

text: The basal lamina is fused to each fiber. Satellite cells, the muscle's stem cells, sit dormant just beneath it.
spoken: The basal lamina is fused to each fiber. Satellite cells, the muscle's stem cells, sit dormant just beneath it.

text: Each nucleus along the fiber manages one stretch of it: the myonuclear domain.
spoken: Each nucleus along the fiber manages one stretch of it: the myonuclear domain.

text: All layers are continuous with each other and the tendon, and pass force sideways: myofascial force transmission.
spoken: All layers are continuous with each other and the tendon, and pass force sideways: myofascial force transmission.

text: Strains usually happen during a forceful eccentric contraction, like the late swing phase of sprinting.
spoken: Strains usually happen during a forceful eccentric contraction, like the late swing phase of sprinting.

text: The hamstring is lengthening under load as the knee extends.
spoken: The hamstring is lengthening under load as the knee extends.

text: Failure usually occurs near the myotendinous junction or the aponeurosis.
spoken: Failure usually occurs near the myotendinous junction or the aponeurosis.

text: The fibers rupture, and the broken ends recoil and retract, leaving a gap.
spoken: The fibers rupture, and the broken ends recoil and retract, leaving a gap.

text: In shearing-type strains the basal lamina sleeves tear too, so regeneration is less orderly and more scar forms.
spoken: In shearing-type strains the basal lamina sleeves tear too, so regeneration is less orderly and more scar forms.

text: Capillaries in the gap tear and bleed.
spoken: Capillaries in the gap tear and bleed.

text: Hematoma: blood fills the gap and clots into a fibrin mesh.
spoken: Hematoma: blood fills the gap and clots into a fibrin mesh.

text: The fibrin net runs in every direction. It is a solid plug, not a hollow box.
spoken: The fibrin net runs in every direction. It is a solid plug, not a hollow box.

text: Calcium pours into torn fibers through the ruptured membrane and stretch-activated channels.
spoken: Calcium pours into torn fibers through the ruptured membrane and stretch-activated channels.

text: Calcium activates calpain. With reactive oxygen species, damage spreads along the fiber: secondary injury.
spoken: Calcium activates calpain. With reactive oxygen species, damage spreads along the fiber: secondary injury.

text: Within hours, a contraction band of hypercontracted filaments reseals the membrane and stops the spread.
spoken: Within hours, a contraction band of hypercontracted filaments reseals the membrane and stops the spread.

text: This happens automatically. It does not depend on the athlete contracting the muscle.
spoken: This happens automatically. It does not depend on the athlete contracting the muscle.

text: Torn vessels and swelling cut off oxygen to the area, which can kill more fibers.
spoken: Torn vessels and swelling cut off oxygen to the area, which can kill more fibers.

text: Clinical tie-in. What limits secondary damage.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. What limits secondary damage.

text: Stop activity right away. Compress and elevate to control bleeding and swelling.
spoken: Stop activity right away. Compress and elevate to control bleeding and swelling.

text: Avoid eccentric loading in the first days.
spoken: Avoid eccentric loading in the first days.

text: Myth to correct: voluntary isometrics in the first hours do not "build" the contraction band. Tension across a fresh tear can widen the gap.
spoken: Myth to correct: voluntary isometrics in the first hours do not build the contraction band. Tension across a fresh tear can widen the gap.

text: Immediate active mobilization in rats produced larger scars and frequent re-rupture. About 5 days of relative rest let granulation tissue bridge the gap first.
spoken: Immediate active mobilization in rats produced larger scars and frequent re-rupture. About 5 days of relative rest let granulation tissue bridge the gap first.

text: No proven treatment blocks the calcium cascade after injury in humans. Pre-exercise L-arginine shows promise as prevention only. Antioxidant supplements have not helped.
spoken: No proven treatment blocks the calcium cascade after injury in humans. Pre-exercise L-arginine shows promise as prevention only. Antioxidant supplements have not helped.

text: Damaged cells release alarm molecules (DAMPs) that call in immune cells.
spoken: Damaged cells release alarm molecules, damps, that call in immune cells.

text: Neutrophils arrive within hours.
spoken: Neutrophils arrive within hours.

text: Pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages follow and dominate the first ~3 days, engulfing necrotic debris.
spoken: Pro-inflammatory M one macrophages follow and dominate the first about 3 days, engulfing necrotic debris.

text: Behind each contraction band the dead segment is cleared, leaving an empty basal-lamina tube.
spoken: Behind each contraction band the dead segment is cleared, leaving an empty basal-lamina tube.

text: TNF, IL-1β and IL-6 also tell satellite cells to wake up and multiply.
spoken: T N F, I L one beta and I L six also tell satellite cells to wake up and multiply.

text: Inflammation here is not only damage. It is the starting signal for regeneration.
spoken: Inflammation here is not only damage. It is the starting signal for regeneration.

text: After eating dead cells (efferocytosis), macrophages reprogram into M2 "repair" macrophages.
spoken: After eating dead cells, efferocytosis,, macrophages reprogram into M two repair macrophages.

text: M2 cells release IL-10, IGF-1 and growth factors that calm inflammation and drive satellite-cell differentiation and fusion.
spoken: M two cells release I L ten, I G F one and growth factors that calm inflammation and drive satellite-cell differentiation and fusion.

text: M1 and M2 are ends of a continuum. Finishing the cleanup triggers the switch, not inflammation simply fading.
spoken: M one and M two are ends of a continuum. Finishing the cleanup triggers the switch, not inflammation simply fading.

text: Repeated re-injury restarts M1 activity and pushes toward chronic inflammation and fibrosis.
spoken: Repeated re-injury restarts M one activity and pushes toward chronic inflammation and fibrosis.

text: NSAIDs block COX enzymes in the injured tissue, which lowers local prostaglandins.
spoken: N-sayds block cox enzymes in the injured tissue, which lowers local prostaglandins.

text: Some of those prostaglandins are signals satellite cells use.
spoken: Some of those prostaglandins are signals satellite cells use.

text: Acetaminophen works mainly in the central nervous system and has little effect on local prostaglandins.
spoken: Acetaminophen works mainly in the central nervous system and has little effect on local prostaglandins.

text: In mice it did not impair regeneration.
spoken: In mice it did not impair regeneration.

text: Clinical tie-in. Pain medication during regeneration.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Pain medication during regeneration.

text: Short-term NSAID use gave small benefits in strength loss, soreness and CK. No human study followed outcomes beyond 14 days.
spoken: Short-term N-sayd use gave small benefits in strength loss, soreness and C K. No human study followed outcomes beyond 14 days.

text: In animals, effects turned negative with longer courses or later timing. Ketorolac at 47 h impaired regeneration in mice, though the macrophage switch was unaffected.
spoken: In animals, effects turned negative with longer courses or later timing. Ketorolac at 47 hours impaired regeneration in mice, though the macrophage switch was unaffected.

text: Conflicting: ibuprofen 1,200 mg/day (2 wk before, 4 wk after) increased satellite-cell activation and sped remodeling at 30 days in an e-stim injury model.
spoken: Conflicting: ibuprofen twelve hundred milligrams a day, 2 weeks before, 4 weeks after, increased satellite-cell activation and sped remodeling at 30 days in an e-stim injury model.

text: Acetaminophen did not impair regeneration in mice.
spoken: Acetaminophen did not impair regeneration in mice.

text: Position: prefer acetaminophen for pain. If an NSAID is used, keep it short. Avoid regular use over several weeks during regeneration. Mind GI, kidney and bleeding risk.
spoken: Position: prefer acetaminophen for pain. If an N-sayd is used, keep it short. Avoid regular use over several weeks during regeneration. Mind G I, kidney and bleeding risk.

text: New capillaries sprout from intact vessels at the edges and grow into the clot and granulation tissue.
spoken: New capillaries sprout from intact vessels at the edges and grow into the clot and granulation tissue.

text: They are visible by about day 3, driven by VEGF released by macrophages.
spoken: They are visible by about day 3, driven by vej-eff released by macrophages.

text: Oxygen delivery is rate-limiting. Regeneration moves only as fast as the supply lines advance.
spoken: Oxygen delivery is rate-limiting. Regeneration moves only as fast as the supply lines advance.

text: The goal is to restore blood flow, not to flood the tissue with oxygen.
spoken: The goal is to restore blood flow, not to flood the tissue with oxygen.

text: Shockwave in rats: one session increased satellite-cell recruitment, proliferation and differentiation.
spoken: Shockwave in rats: one session increased satellite-cell recruitment, proliferation and differentiation.

text: Treated muscle reached at day 4 what untreated muscle reached at day 7. Controlled human trials in acute strains are lacking.
spoken: Treated muscle reached at day 4 what untreated muscle reached at day 7. Controlled human trials in acute strains are lacking.

text: Clinical tie-in. Supporting the supply lines.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Supporting the supply lines.

text: Support blood flow with pain-guided early movement, swelling control and nicotine avoidance.
spoken: Support blood flow with pain-guided early movement, swelling control and nicotine avoidance.

text: Shockwave (ESWT): faster regeneration in rats. Reviews describe VEGF- and eNOS-driven vessel growth. Controlled human trials in acute strains are lacking.
spoken: Shockwave, E S W T,: faster regeneration in rats. Reviews describe vej-eff- and e-noss-driven vessel growth. Controlled human trials in acute strains are lacking.

text: Hyperbaric oxygen improved oxygenation and regeneration in rat contusions. Human data are lacking, and it is not standard care.
spoken: Hyperbaric oxygen improved oxygenation and regeneration in rat contusions. Human data are lacking, and it is not standard care.

text: Fibrin and fibronectin from the clot cross-link into granulation tissue, a primary extracellular matrix.
spoken: Fibrin and fibronectin from the clot cross-link into granulation tissue, a primary extracellular matrix.

text: It anchors fibroblasts, which lay down tenascin-C and fibronectin, then type III collagen.
spoken: It anchors fibroblasts, which lay down tenascin C and fibronectin, then type three collagen.

text: New capillary loops make the tissue red and grainy, which is where "granulation" comes from.
spoken: New capillary loops make the tissue red and grainy, which is where granulation comes from.

text: Type III fibers start out disorganized. Type I, which provides most tensile strength, comes later.
spoken: Type three fibers start out disorganized. Type one, which provides most tensile strength, comes later.

text: The plug fills the gap stump to stump. In week one it holds, but tears easily.
spoken: The plug fills the gap stump to stump. In week one it holds, but tears easily.

text: Activated satellite cells switch on MyoD and Myf5 and multiply as myoblasts.
spoken: Activated satellite cells switch on myo D and myf five and multiply as myoblasts.

text: They multiply inside the empty basal-lamina tunnels.
spoken: They multiply inside the empty basal-lamina tunnels.

text: They switch on myogenin and fuse into a multinucleated myotube.
spoken: They switch on myogenin and fuse into a multinucleated myotube.

text: Each nucleus can only support a limited length of fiber, so a long fiber needs many nuclei.
spoken: Each nucleus can only support a limited length of fiber, so a long fiber needs many nuclei.

text: Some satellite cells self-renew, restocking the reserve for future injuries.
spoken: Some satellite cells self-renew, restocking the reserve for future injuries.

text: Myotubes become new fibers or fuse onto the surviving stumps.
spoken: Myotubes become new fibers or fuse onto the surviving stumps.

text: Clinical tie-in. Electrical stimulation.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Electrical stimulation.

text: Rat strain model: low-frequency e-stim, 20 Hz, 30 minutes twice daily, started at day 5.
spoken: Rat strain model: low-frequency e-stim, 20 hertz, 30 minutes twice daily, started at day 5.

text: It increased MyoD and myogenin and produced more mature, well-ordered fibers.
spoken: It increased myo D and myogenin and produced more mature, well-ordered fibers.

text: Day 5 was chosen on purpose: after granulation tissue had bridged the gap.
spoken: Day 5 was chosen on purpose: after granulation tissue had bridged the gap.

text: From about day 5, regenerating stumps send out branches that pierce into both sides of the scar.
spoken: From about day 5, regenerating stumps send out branches that pierce into both sides of the scar.

text: Each branch anchors to scar collagen through new mini-myotendinous junctions.
spoken: Each branch anchors to scar collagen through new mini-myotendinous junctions.

text: Day 14: the scar condenses, and the fibers close most of the gap.
spoken: Day 14: the scar condenses, and the fibers close most of the gap.

text: Day 21: fibers from both sides interlace, with a thin seam of scar between them.
spoken: Day 21: fibers from both sides interlace, with a thin seam of scar between them.

text: Nerves regrow along old paths and new NMJs form. Regeneration peaks ~2 weeks and slows by ~4 weeks.
spoken: Nerves regrow along old paths and new neuromuscular junctions form. Regeneration peaks about 2 weeks and slows by about 4 weeks.

text: Small gap with controlled scar: many fingers interlock.
spoken: Small gap with controlled scar: many fingers interlock.

text: Large gap with excessive scar: a dense wall blocks the fibers, which stop and curl.
spoken: Large gap with excessive scar: a dense wall blocks the fibers, which stop and curl.

text: Clinical tie-in. Tipping the balance toward muscle.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Tipping the balance toward muscle.

text: Keep the gap small with early compression and protection.
spoken: Keep the gap small with early compression and protection.

text: Relative rest for about the first 3–5 days, then progressive, pain-guided loading: isometric, then isotonic, then dynamic.
spoken: Relative rest for about the first 3 to 5 days, then progressive, pain-guided loading: isometric, then isotonic, then dynamic.

text: Avoid prolonged immobilization. It leads to a larger, more disorganized, contracted scar.
spoken: Avoid prolonged immobilization. It leads to a larger, more disorganized, contracted scar.

text: Too much TGF-β1 drives fibroblasts toward dense scar. Antifibrotic agents and PRP are experimental.
spoken: Too much T G F beta one drives fibroblasts toward dense scar. Antifibrotic agents and P R P are experimental.

text: New fibers grow thicker, move their nuclei to the edge, and line up their sarcomeres. Capillaries are pruned back.
spoken: New fibers grow thicker, move their nuclei to the edge, and line up their sarcomeres. Capillaries are pruned back.

text: Collagen shifts from type III to type I, thickens, cross-links, and aligns with the direction of pull.
spoken: Collagen shifts from type three to type one, thickens, cross-links, and aligns with the direction of pull.

text: Fibroblasts become myofibroblasts, which pull on the collagen like tiny winches. The scar contracts.
spoken: Fibroblasts become myofibroblasts, which pull on the collagen like tiny winches. The scar contracts.

text: Remodeling lasts months. In human strains, MRI still shows active repair at 6 months, after return to sport.
spoken: Remodeling lasts months. In human strains, M R I still shows active repair at 6 months, after return to sport.

text: Loaded muscle: aligned collagen, thin scar.
spoken: Loaded muscle: aligned collagen, thin scar.

text: Immobilized muscle: a tangled, shortened scar.
spoken: Immobilized muscle: a tangled, shortened scar.

text: Clinical tie-in. Speeding the type III → type I shift.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Speeding the type three to type one shift.

text: Progressive mechanical loading drives collagen synthesis and alignment.
spoken: Progressive mechanical loading drives collagen synthesis and alignment.

text: Ensure adequate protein and energy intake.
spoken: Ensure adequate protein and energy intake.

text: Avoid smoking and long courses of NSAIDs or corticosteroids.
spoken: Avoid smoking and long courses of N-sayds or corticosteroids.

text: Cross-linking runs on biological time. Loading improves quality and alignment more than it shortens the calendar.
spoken: Cross-linking runs on biological time. Loading improves quality and alignment more than it shortens the calendar.

text: Carla Stecco's group describes densification of the hyaluronan-rich layer between fascial sheets.
spoken: Carla Stecco's group describes densification of the hyaluronan-rich layer between fascial sheets.

text: After trauma, overuse, disuse or inflammation, the layer becomes more viscous, without true fibrosis having to be present.
spoken: After trauma, overuse, disuse or inflammation, the layer becomes more viscous, without true fibrosis having to be present.

text: Gliding is reduced, and free nerve endings may become irritated.
spoken: Gliding is reduced, and free nerve endings may become irritated.

text: Two depths: the collagen scar inside the muscle is permanent. Densified gel is proposed to be reversible.
spoken: Two depths: the collagen scar inside the muscle is permanent. Densified gel is proposed to be reversible.

text: Movement and manual shear are proposed to restore gliding. Direct human evidence for HA changes is limited.
spoken: Movement and manual shear are proposed to restore gliding. Direct human evidence for hyaluronan changes is limited.

text: The muscle model and the fascial model complement each other.
spoken: The muscle model and the fascial model complement each other.

text: Clinical tie-in. Fascial work: evidence status.
spoken: Clinical tie-in. Fascial work: evidence status.

text: Myofascial release is consistently associated with short-term improvements in pain and range of motion.
spoken: Myofascial release is consistently associated with short-term improvements in pain and range of motion.

text: Long-term functional outcomes and direct structural change in fascia are inconsistent.
spoken: Long-term functional outcomes and direct structural change in fascia are inconsistent.

text: Best supported as an adjunct that helps athletes move and engage in active rehab, not as stand-alone treatment.
spoken: Best supported as an adjunct that helps athletes move and engage in active rehab, not as stand-alone treatment.

text: Proposed calcium–hyaluronan feedback loop; fascial stiffening may impair regeneration, so treat both muscle and fascia.
spoken: Proposed calcium hyaluronan feedback loop; fascial stiffening may impair regeneration, so treat both muscle and fascia.

text: Timing: gentle work and movement around the injury in subacute and remodeling phases. No aggressive deep work on the tear in week 1.
spoken: Timing: gentle work and movement around the injury in subacute and remodeling phases. No aggressive deep work on the tear in week 1.

text: The scar is not muscle. It is stiffer, does not contract, and changes how force passes through the muscle.
spoken: The scar is not muscle. It is stiffer, does not contract, and changes how force passes through the muscle.

text: The folded myotendinous junction may never fully return. Atrophy and fat infiltration develop.
spoken: The folded myotendinous junction may never fully return. Atrophy and fat infiltration develop.

text: Neural inhibition: the injured muscle is under-activated, especially in eccentric work at long lengths.
spoken: Neural inhibition: the injured muscle is under-activated, especially in eccentric work at long lengths.

text: Returning to sport before the tissue has matured contributes to the high re-injury rate.
spoken: Returning to sport before the tissue has matured contributes to the high re-injury rate.

text: Time the stimulus to the biology.
spoken: Time the stimulus to the biology.

text: 0–48 h: stop, compress, elevate, protect. No eccentric loading. Acetaminophen preferred.
spoken: Zero to forty-eight hours: stop, compress, elevate, protect. No eccentric loading. Acetaminophen preferred.

text: Days 2–5: pain-free isometrics. Avoid both immobilization and aggressive loading.
spoken: Days 2 to 5: pain-free isometrics. Avoid both immobilization and aggressive loading.

text: Days 5–21: progressive isotonic, then dynamic loading. Gentle fascial work around the site.
spoken: Days 5 to 21: progressive isotonic, then dynamic loading. Gentle fascial work around the site.

text: Weeks 3–12: lengthening and eccentric work at long muscle lengths. Criteria-based return to sport.
spoken: Weeks 3 to 12: lengthening and eccentric work at long muscle lengths. Criteria-based return to sport.

text: Months 3–6+: keep up eccentric strengthening, like Nordic curls, after return to play.
spoken: Months 3 to 6 and beyond: keep up eccentric strengthening, like Nordic curls, after return to play.

text: Healing is a race between muscle regrowth and scar, inside a fascial system that has to keep gliding.
spoken: Healing is a race between muscle regrowth and scar, inside a fascial system that has to keep gliding.

text: Protect the wet cement, feed the supply lines, load the rebuilders, align the rope, and keep the layers sliding.
spoken: Protect the wet cement, feed the supply lines, load the rebuilders, align the rope, and keep the layers sliding.

text: The sources cited in this film are listed on screen.
spoken: The sources cited in this film are listed on screen.
